title: Mitigate neighbor-cache (ARP/NDP) surge during private orchestrator upgrades and follow-up action items
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During the Feb 12 private orchestrator rolling upgrade in eu-west-1, an upgrade wave caused coordinated agent reconnects leading to an NDP/ARP neighbor-cache surge on customer VPCs. The surge overflowed per-node neighbor tables on some hypervisors and triggered control plane connection failures for ~22% of nodes in the wave. Customer-facing symptoms: intermittent API timeouts for private clusters, upgrade rollbacks, and degraded KV cache hit rates. This ticket captures the post-incident action items, proposed mitigations, owners, timelines, and links to artifacts.
incident_root_causes: Coordinated agent restarts during blue-green upgrade wave triggered simultaneous ARP/NDP refreshes (neighbor discovery storm)
Hypervisor neighbor table capacity wasn't surfaced; eviction behavior caused transient blackholes as nodes re-appeared with changed MACs
Agent reconnection logic performed aggressive immediate retries without jitter/backoff, amplifying network churn
No pre-upgrade impact guardrail to limit parallel agent restarts per rack/availability zone for private deployments
short_term_mitigations_done: Paused remaining upgrade waves and rolled back the active wave to stable image (completed 2026-02-12 18:24 UTC)
Applied temporary per-host neighbor cache guard (kernel sysctl adjustments) on most impacted hosts via ops automation
Disabled aggressive agent reconnection path (hotfix 2026-02-13) to add 200-500ms randomized jitter between retries
Added temporary alert on neighbor table exhaustion in Grafana (dashboard: private-networking/neighbor-table-overview)
Ran targeted replays of canary traffic and validated control plane reconnection stability in a staging VPC
action_items: (Owner: Miguel Torres) Implement staggered upgrade waves with per-rack concurrency limit and randomized start offsets. Update orchestrator to support per-subnet wave targeting. Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-03-08. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4021

(Owner: Priya Desai) Add exponential backoff + jitter to agent reconnect logic; expose policy via agent config for private installs. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-02-28. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/1198

(Owner: Network SRE - Tomas Müller) Add neighbor-table capacity telemetry (per-hypervisor and per-host) and an automatic pre-upgrade check to fail fast if capacity < 20% headroom. Estimate: 4 points. Due: 2026-03-12. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/private-networking

(Owner: Security & Compliance - Lina Chen) Document and publish escalation runbook for neighbor-cache saturations (runbook: Confluence/private/neighbor-cache-runbook) and add it to oncall playbooks. Estimate: 2 points. Due: 2026-03-01

(Owner: Infra - Omar Rahman) Add kernel tuning recommendations to private deploy docs: neighbor GC thresholds, conntrack slab sizing, and sysctl recipes for large VPCs. Create a preflight script that validates host settings. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-10

(Owner: Observability - Fatima Khan) Create an SLO-level alert that ties control plane reconnect latency to backend error budget and surfaces customer clusters affected. Add a synthetic probe for private control plane API post-upgrade. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-05

(Owner: Product - Miguel Torres) Add an orchestration flag 'upgrade-safety-mode' that defaults to conservative concurrency for private installs and is exposed in Console. UX spec: https://confluence.redwood/private/upgrade-safety-mode. Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-03-15
risk_and_tradeoffs: Conservative default concurrency will increase upgrade duration for large fleets; tradeoff accepted for stability in private customer networks
Kernel tuning suggestions may not be applicable for all customer hypervisor vendors; we will provide optionality and preflight checks
Agent reconnect throttle makes failover slower under genuine network partitions; mitigated by balanced backoff windows and health checks
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator supports per-subnet/rack upgrade concurrency with randomized offsets and default conservative settings for private installs
Agent binary includes configurable exponential backoff with unit tests and E2E test exercising reconnect jitter under failure injection
New Grafana panels show neighbor-table headroom and trigger automated preflight abort for upgrades if headroom < threshold
Runbook published and validated in next oncall rotation (tabletop exercise completed)
